'''Himarimã''' is the presumed language of the [[Uncontacted peoples|uncontacted]] [[Hi-Merimã people]] in [[Amazonas (Brazilian state)|Amazonas]], [[Brazil]]. A contact may have happened in 2007.<ref>{{e25|hir}}</ref> A wordlist was recorded, but was later lost.<ref>{{Citation |last=Campbell |first=Lyle |title=Indigenous Languages of South America |date=2024-06-25 |work=The Indigenous Languages of the Americas |pages=182–279 |url=https://academic.oup.com/book/57386/chapter/464719092 |access-date=2025-04-16 |edition=1 |publisher=Oxford University PressNew York |language=en |doi=10.1093/oso/9780197673461.003.0004 |isbn=978-0-19-767346-1|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The language is believed to be [[Arawan languages|Arawán]] per testimonies from the [[Suruwahá language|Suruwahá]] and [[Banawá language|Banawá]].<ref>Hammarström (2015) Ethnologue 16/17/18th editions: a comprehensive review: online appendices</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.1 - Himarimã |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/hima1247 |access-date=2025-04-16 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref>
